hints.title: Ratio Sorting Strategy
hints.text: Sort workers according to their ratio of wage over capacity.

hints.title: Bottleneck Ratio Multiplication
hints.text: The total payment equals the maximum wage-to-quality ratio in the group multiplied by the sum of qualities.

hints.title: Greedy Smallest Quality Maintenance
hints.text: Iterate workers in increasing ratio order while retaining the k smallest qualities, ejecting the maximum quality whenever the group size exceeds k.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
from typing import List
import heapq

class Solution:
    def mincostToHireWorkers(self, quality: List[int], wage: List[int], k: int) -> float:
        workers = sorted([(w / q, q) for w, q in zip(wage, quality)])
        max_heap = []
        sum_quality = 0
        min_cost = float('inf')

        for ratio, q in workers:
            heapq.heappush(max_heap, -q)
            sum_quality += q
            if len(max_heap) > k:
                sum_quality += heapq.heappop(max_heap)
            if len(max_heap) == k:
                min_cost = min(min_cost, ratio * sum_quality)

        return min_cost
```

complexity.notes: Ratio sorting followed by bounded priority heap tracking smallest qualities.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Combinatorial selection of K workers takes exponential O(C(N, K)) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Auxiliary heap of size K requires O(K) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Realize that ratio order fixes the baseline pay multiplier for all preceding workers.
